title: K-Veritas Go 用签名 PDF 证明代码跑过，但信任根仍是软肋
summary: K-Veritas Go 通过签名 PDF 和硬件遥测为计算过程提供可验证出处，但 HN 评论者质疑其防伪能力，核心矛盾在于信任根是否真的不可伪造。
opening: K-Veritas Go 试图解决一个真实痛点：当审阅者无法或不愿重跑代码时，如何证明报告中的结果确实由特定代码在特定硬件上产生。它给出的答案是“执行见证”——在计算过程中采集遥测数据，生成密码学签名的 PDF。但 HN 上的质疑直指要害：如果攻击者控制运行环境，签名只能证明作者签署了报告，不能证明报告内容真实。这个工具的价值和边界，都藏在信任根的设计里。
core_experience:
K-Veritas Go 的使用流程围绕几个命令展开：init 初始化项目，run 执行计算并采集遥测，seal 生成签名 PDF 报告，verify 验证报告完整性。用户可以在代码中通过 stdout 打印协议行来记录指标、阶段、声明、模型卡等，这些内容会被纳入报告。后台采样器以约 10Hz 频率记录进程级遥测，包括 CPU、内存、上下文切换、页错误和 GPU 利用率。

报告的核心是 HMCA（执行连贯性）评分。它不看报告结果，只看多个遥测通道是否像同一进程的影子一样共同波动，给出 PASS、WARN、FAIL 或 N/A 的判定。另一个关键机制是计算成本证明：检查声明的 FLOPs 是否超出硬件物理极限，并设置时间、能量和内存的边界。报告支持三种披露级别（redacted、names、open），默认 redacted，但完整性始终被提交。选择性披露证明允许只揭示某个文件或记录，而不暴露其他内容。

从产品角度看，K-Veritas Go 试图把“代码确实跑过”变成一种可验证的声明，而不是依赖审阅者重跑。它跨平台，但文件/子进程活动映射和每进程硬件归因仅限 Linux，其他平台回退到系统级读数。
why_it_works:
K-Veritas Go 的有效性来自两个设计选择。第一，HMCA 是度量盲的：它不关心报告声称的结果是什么，只关心遥测数据是否呈现出一致的行为模式。真实运行会自然产生 CPU、内存和 I/O 之间的相关性，而伪造数据很难在所有维度上保持连贯。这增加了伪造的难度，因为攻击者不仅要伪造结果，还要伪造一组在多个维度上相互吻合的遥测数据。

第二，计算成本证明利用硬件物理极限作为不可逾越的约束。任何声称超过峰值 FLOPs 或能量消耗的计算都会被标记为 FABRICATION-IMPOSSIBLE。物理定律无法被篡改，这比单纯依赖软件日志更难以绕过。签名和 Merkle 树保证了报告内容不可篡改，而选择性披露则允许在保护隐私的同时提供可验证的证据。对于 AI 产品经理而言，这意味着可以低成本地为模型训练或推理过程附加可信的出处证明，而无需让审阅者重新运行昂贵的计算。
boundaries:
HN 评论者的质疑切中了信任根问题：如果攻击者能控制运行环境，他们可能伪造遥测数据或签名，除非在安全 enclave 中运行。K-Veritas Go 的签名只能证明作者签署了报告，不能证明报告内容真实。这是所有软件级证明工具的共同局限。

HMCA 本身也有误判风险。轻量运行可能因遥测数据不足而得到 N/A，而精心构造的伪造可能通过连贯性检查。平台限制也很明显：文件/子进程活动映射和每进程硬件归因仅限 Linux，其他平台回退到系统级读数，降低了精确性。性能开销未明确量化，后台采样可能对计算密集型任务产生额外负载。多进程或分布式计算支持不明确，可能无法覆盖复杂工作流。
personal_judgment:
K-Veritas Go 代表了一类新兴的“可验证计算”工具，它试图在软件层面解决信任问题，但根本挑战在于信任根。如果用户完全控制运行环境，任何软件级证明都可能被绕过。除非结合硬件信任根（如 TPM、SGX）或第三方见证，否则该工具更适合作为威慑或低风险场景的辅助证据，而非绝对证明。

对于 AI 产品经理，其价值在于提供了一种轻量级的出处记录和审计线索，尤其在需要向非技术利益相关者展示模型训练过程时。但产品设计上应明确其安全边界，避免过度承诺“防篡改”。

transferable_methods.name: 物理边界证明
transferable_methods.principle: 利用硬件物理极限（如峰值 FLOPs、能量消耗）作为不可逾越的约束，检查声明是否可能由给定硬件产生。这比单纯依赖软件日志更难以伪造，因为物理定律无法被篡改。
transferable_methods.applies_when: 适用于需要验证计算资源声明（如训练成本、推理延迟）的场景，尤其是当审阅者无法直接访问运行环境时。

transferable_methods.name: 度量盲的连贯性检查
transferable_methods.principle: 不检查报告结果本身，而是分析多个遥测通道是否呈现出一致的行为模式（如 CPU 和内存使用同时上升）。真实运行会自然产生这种相关性，而伪造数据很难在所有维度上保持连贯。
transferable_methods.applies_when: 适用于需要检测伪造或重放攻击的场景，例如验证实验是否真的执行过，或监控 AI 模型推理是否在声称的硬件上运行。

product_takeaway: AI 产品经理在设计可验证或审计功能时，应明确信任根的位置：软件级证明只能提供辅助证据，真正的信任需要硬件信任根或第三方见证。同时，度量盲的连贯性检查是一种值得借鉴的防伪思路，它不依赖结果正确性，而是关注过程一致性。

sources.title: kveritas-go
sources.excerpt: # K-Veritas Go Tamper-evident verification for computational experiments. It binds a published result to the exact code, hardware, and time that produced it, in a cryptographically signed PDF anyone can verify. Works with any language, zero runtime dependencies, single static binary. **Platform.** Verify, seal, proofs, checkout, benchmark artifacts, provenance, and disclosure levels are cross-platform. The file/subprocess **activity map** and **per-process hardware attribution** are Linux-only today; elsewhere they fall back to system-wide readings. ## Install Prebuilt binary: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/27-GROUP/kveritas-releases/raw/main/bin/kveritas-linux-amd64 -o kveritas chmod +x kveritas && sudo mv kveritas /usr/local/bin/ ``` Binaries: `kveritas-{linux,darwin,windows}-{amd64,arm64}`. Or build from source (Go 1.22+): `make build`. ## Quick start ```bash kveritas init # start a session (redacted by default) kveritas run -- python train.py --epochs 90 # run under kveritas (any command) kveritas run -- python evaluate.py kveritas seal --output report.pdf # signed PDF (+ bundle at --disclosure open) kveritas verify report.pdf # verify (add --offline to skip the server) ``` ## Protocol lines Print these to stdout in any language; everything captured is bound into the signed record. | Line | Purpose | |---|---| | `KVERITAS_METRIC name=<id> value=<float> [step=<label>]` | Record a metric. | | `KVERITAS_PHASE name=<phase>` | Mark a phase boundary (hardware snapshot). | | `KVERITAS_CLAIM metric=<id> value=<float>` | Commit a headline claim. | | `KVERITAS_INPUT src=seed:<value>` | Commit a random seed. | | `KVERITAS_MODEL params=<int> arch=<name> precision=<fp16\|bf16\|fp32>` | Model card (feeds compute-cost). | | `KVERITAS_WORKLOAD dataset_size=<int> epochs=<float> batch_size=<int> [seq_len=<int>]` | Workload card. | | `KVERITAS_ARTIFACT role=model\|dataset [name=<ref>] path=<file> visibility=public\|private` | Attest a model or dataset. | Common metrics are also auto-detected (Keras history, sklearn CV, metric-like locals), so simple runs need no lines. ## HMCA (execution coherence) Metric-blind. It never looks at the reported result. During the run a background sampler records per-process telemetry (CPU, memory, context switches, page faults, CPU frequency, I/O, and, when a GPU is used, its utilization, memory, power, temperature) at about 10 Hz. At seal time HMCA scores whether those channels co-fluctuate as shadows of one process: a genuine run drives them all from one activity, a fabricated or replayed trace does not. Verdict is `PASS` (coherent), `WARN`, `FAIL` (incoherent), or `N/A` (too little telemetry to judge). A light run is judged on the activity it has, never penalized for being light. The web verifier renders the channels over time. ## Compute-cost attestation When a run declares a model card, seal produces a certificate checking the declared FLOPs against what the hardware could physically deliver. | Bound | Impossible when | |---|---| | Time | declared FLOPs exceed GPU peak x GPU-active seconds plus CPU peak x CPU core-seconds | | Energy | declared FLOPs exceed measured GPU joules divided by the minimum energy per FLOP | | Memory | declared weights exceed observed GPU memory (soft) | The time bound sums every device, so it fires whether the work ran on GPU, CPU, or both (a 175B model declared on an idle CPU is caught). Bounds are generous, so honest runs pass; no card or no telemetry is `N/A`. A hard violation is `FABRICATION-IMPOSSIBLE`, bound into the signature. ## Provenance and disclosure Each run is a signed timeline of content-addressed snapshots (source state at run start, each phase, and run end, plus what changed), Merkle-linked and bound into the signature. You choose per session how much is revealed; this controls disclosure only, integrity is always committed. | Level | Flag | Report shows | |---|---|---| | redacted (default) | `kveritas init` | Pseudonyms, no names, no content | | names | `--show-names` | Real file names, no content | | open | `--disclosure open` | Real names + a checkout bundle (code) | A redacted report reveals nothing sensitive (no code, names, data, weights, command line, or salt); the server only ever receives a hash. Patterns in `.kveritasignore` keep files out of any bundle; a withheld file is still committed as a hash-only leaf and listed as withheld, so it cannot be silently dropped. ## Selective-disclosure proofs Reveal one file was in a signed snapshot without exposing the others: ```bash kveritas prove report.pdf src/train.py kveritas verify-proof kveritas-proof-train.py.json ``` For agent sessions, prove one recorded prompt or output against its committed hash, leaving every other entry a hash: ```bash kveritas harness-prove session.json 1 --input prompt.txt -o proof.json kveritas verify-harness-proof proof.json ``` Select the entry by index or `--tool-use-id`; reveal the prompt with `--input` or the response with `--output-content`. ## Chec

sources.title: Show HN: Prove your code produced your claims without making reviewers rerun it
sources.excerpt:
The readme has a lot of words but still does not clearly explain what this does or what you'd use it for. The best I can gather is that this captures telemetry while you're running some computationally-expensive job, and checks that the resource usage roughly matches what it's supposed to be. But what does "Tamper-evident" mean? I assume you sign with your own private key? What exactly prevents the data from being faked?
It didn't sound very convincing. It doesn't really prove anything other than the author signed the report. Unless the auditing is running from a secure enclave/core that the user has no access to, it can't do what is claimed on the tin.
